name: deploy
description: Run a pgmi deployment against a database and return the structured result. Resolves like `pgmi deploy`: arguments override the server's environment (PGMI_CONNECTION_STRING, DATABASE_URL, PG*), which overrides the project's pgmi.yaml (connection, params, timeout). Unlike `pgmi deploy`, the project .env is not read; pass params or set them in the server's environment. Keep secrets in the environment (PGMI_PARAM_<NAME> becomes parameter <name>, below a params file) or a params file, not in arguments. overwrite=true DROPS the target database: it additionally requires confirmDatabaseName to equal the resolved database.

confirmDatabaseName.description: Required when overwrite=true: repeat the target database name exactly. A mismatch aborts before any connection is made.

connection.description: PostgreSQL connection string: URI, libpq keyword/value (host=... dbname=...), or ADO.NET. Default: environment, then pgmi.yaml

database.description: Target database name. Default: the connection's database, then pgmi.yaml

maintenanceDatabase.description: Database used for CREATE/DROP DATABASE (default: resolved like pgmi deploy, usually "postgres")

overwrite.description: Drop and recreate the target database before deploying (destructive)

params.description: Deployment parameters, available as current_setting('pgmi.key'); override paramsFile and pgmi.yaml, like --param

paramsFile.description: Params file path (KEY=VALUE lines), or an array of them; later files win, like --params-file. Stdin (-) is not accepted

path.description: Path to the pgmi project directory (contains deploy.sql)

timeout.description: Catastrophic-failure timeout, e.g. "3m" (default: pgmi.yaml, then 3m). Use "0" for no limit

verbose.description: Like pgmi deploy -v: RAISE DEBUG from deploy.sql and tests reaches notices

created.description: True when this deploy created the database; on a routine deploy it usually means a mistyped database name

executionUnits.description: Units deploy.sql split into at its first top-level COMMIT

exitCode.description: The exit code `pgmi deploy` would have returned

filesLoaded.description: Project files loaded into the session

ignoredPaths.description: Each ignored path and the rule that left it out

path.description: The ignored path in ./ form; a directory ends with /

notices.description: The deploy's notice stream: the first 50, up to 200 WARNINGs from the middle, and the last 150

detail.description: The notice's DETAIL; absent when it has none

hint.description: The notice's HINT, often what to do next; absent when it has none

noticesTruncated.description: Notices dropped from the middle of the stream, WARNINGs beyond the first 200 included; absent when none were

pathsIgnored.description: Paths left out by the built-in exclusions and .pgmiignore; an ignored directory counts once

status.description: "success" — a failure is returned as an MCP error result

exitCode.description: Exit code the CLI would return for this failure

failedFile.description: The file that failed: a project or test file, or deploy.sql

failedFileCandidates.description: Every SQL file holding the failing text, when more than one does; failedFile is the first

phase.description: test when the failure is in a test or fixture under __test__/, deploy for any other failure of deploy.sql

script.description: The file the failure was placed in: a project or test file, or deploy.sql

scriptExpanded.description: True when line refers to the macro-expanded script, not the file on disk

sqlstate.description: PostgreSQL SQLSTATE, when the failure came from the server
